facts.fact: A consultancy (Manager General Consulting) presented the Colloc-Pay platform to the Ntoum commune and the Komo-Mondah departmental council on 2026-06-19; no adoption is stated, and the platform is described as digitising and geolocating operators, digitising communal assets and enabling electronic payment of taxes.

facts.fact: The commune of Owendo signed an agreement with the Direction générale des Impôts on 2026-04-29 to implement the national Digitax application for municipal taxes; implementation is announced, one commune named.
Digitax is the Direction générale des Impôts' platform; the DGI will align the Owendo municipal agents' taxpayer directory with its own and parameterise the forms, per the 2026-04-29 agreement.
Owendo and the DGI signed the Digitax partnership on 2026-04-29, with payment by bank transfer and mobile money and automatic taxpayer certificates planned.

systems.tiers: national tax platform; agreed for Owendo commune's municipal taxes (2026-04-29)

facts.fact: The Libreville city hall launched a pilot of digitised municipal revenue collection on 2025-07-29; one commune is named.

The pilot platform is described as resting on a geolocated taxpayer file, online declaration and payment, automatic tax and penalty amounts and a dashboard showing who is up to date on which taxes; these are the vendor's stated design at launch, 2025-07-29.
The platform is developed by the company GTI Gabon, inspired by the national Digitax platform, for the Libreville city hall; launched 2025-07-29.
Libreville launched the revenue-digitalisation pilot on 2025-07-29.

facts.fact: Libreville city hall presented e-Taxe municipale on 2026-10-30, a platform to declare and pay municipal taxes and fees online, in service since 2026-06-12 and said by the municipality to be 95% operational.

Medias241 reports the Libreville city hall's E-Tax platform, launched 12 June 2026, has enrolled nearly 2,000 market traders in 15 markets, records over 4,000 transactions and gives the city a register of active traders, with payments going directly to the municipal Treasury.
